exercise.name: Barbell Lying Row on Rack
aliases: Prone barbell row on a high bench

reference.title: Barbell Lying Row on Rack
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the bar comes up to the bench, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: the chest stays on the pad and the bar touches the bench each rep.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep touches the bench with a pause.

cues.text: Lie face down on a high flat bench inside a rack, chin past the end; bar on the safety pins below, overhand grip about shoulder width.
Drive the elbows back toward the hips and pull the bar up to the bench under the lower chest.
Touch the bench and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Set the bar on the pins for a moment; stay flat on the bench.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest and hips on the pad; lighten the bar.
Touch the bench every rep and straighten the arms at the bottom.
Pull the shoulder blades back, not up.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the bar onto the pins
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and set it down quietly.

kinematics.norm: Chest-supported rows remove most of the lower-back load of a bent-over row (Fenwick 2009 compared rowing exercises)
Shoulder-width grip with the elbows close works the lats and mid back (Lehman 2004)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Set up the bench so it cannot tip, and the safety pins so the bar is easy to reach and to set down.
Climb on and off the high bench carefully; have the bar on the pins while you get set.
Shoulder pain: narrow the grip and keep the elbows closer to the body.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower bench and lighter plates if the arms cannot hang.
progressions: Pause with the bar on the bench.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Extends the shoulder behind the trunk.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Holds the upper arm turned out.

muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder blades; no shrug.
